sector:economics.overview: Economics brings five things to making AI go well: the political economy of power concentration and lock-in, the economics of transformative AI (windfalls, public finance, labour markets), institutional designs for commons, cooperatives and public AI, organised labour, and the macroprudential toolkit that financial supervisors use to watch whole systems of correlated agents. The map has 56 organisations with economics as their home tradition (6 core, 8 bridge, 40 adjacent, 2 potential), and another 62 draw on it as a secondary tradition, including core groups such as forethought, alignment-of-complex-systems-research-group, meaning-alignment-institute, ai-objectives-institute and future-of-life-foundation. The main actors are unions (17 labour entries), commons and public-AI groups (17), financial-stability bodies (5 of the 8 bridge entries) and a small x-risk cluster on power concentration (formation-research, longview-philanthropy, post-agi-workshop-series). The tradition sits well away from the core: 40 of the 56 are adjacent, 35 work by pushing ideas into institutions, only 2 use a catastrophic framing (convergence-analysis, kira-center), and just 3 are on the aisafety.com map.
sector:economics.missing: Nothing on the map carries economics into the AI systems themselves or into the agent economies now being built. The economics x agency, values and ai_status cells are empty, only 2 of 56 entries tag multi-agent AI, and the map has no competition authority, industrial-organisation (IO) economist or market-design group, even though LLM pricing agents already collude in experiments and companies are building agent payment rails. Two taxonomy examples for this tradition, EconTAI at the University of Virginia and the Stanford Digital Economy Lab, are also absent from the index, which looks like a pipeline artefact and should be fixed before publishing.

cell_notes.note: Two entries (ostrom-workshop, openresearch). This is mostly an artefact of the search, with a real opening inside it. Economics engages with AI so heavily that many relevant bodies already run an AI programme and land in adjacent. But the discovery notes name pools that nobody swept: IO economists and competition authorities (none on the map), market and mechanism-design labs, development economists and resource-governance bodies, sovereign wealth funds, and cash-transfer researchers such as GiveDirectly (named only as openresearch's partner). The investor-stewardship sweep (CFA Institute, NBIM, PRI) stopped when the search budget ran out. A targeted pass would probably add 10-20 entries. The real opening is that these pools hold working methods and have had no contact with AI safety.

Six entries, all political economy (formation-research, longview-philanthropy, post-agi-workshop-series) or TAI economics (windfall-trust, convergence-analysis, kira-center). Commons and cooperatives have no core entry, and nor does organised labour. That gap is real: no cooperative, commons or labour body treats AI going well as its mission. The low total is partly an artefact, since EconTAI and the Stanford Digital Economy Lab are taxonomy examples but are missing from the index. A cheap move for int/a on the commons side: the two 'cooperative AI' communities, platform-cooperativism-consortium (democratic ownership) and the game-theoretic one (foundations-of-cooperative-ai-lab, CAIF), have had almost no contact, and one convening could bring them together.

Eight entries, but five of them are financial-stability bodies (financial-stability-board, bank-for-international-settlements-and-its-finan, bank-of-england, european-systemic-risk-board, systemic-risk-centre-london-school-of-economics). Each of the other sub-traditions has exactly one: commons (funding-the-commons), labour (united-tech-and-allied-workers-with-unite-the-un) and power (equiano-institute). The thin labour and commons cells are real: organised labour reaches AI safety through a single union branch's campaign at one lab. Several adjacent organisations are one framing away from bridge, notably institute-for-the-future-of-work, mit-stone-center-on-inequality-and-shaping-the-f and open-markets-institute, whose idea of 'AI lock-in' is close to formation-research's.

sector:economics.key_insight: 52 of the 56 economics organisations (93%) tag power, but only 2 tag multi-agent AI and none tag agency, values or AI's moral status. Economics on this map treats AI as something that moves wealth and power between humans, almost never as a population of strategic economic actors, although IO economics, mechanism design and macroprudential supervision are tools built for exactly that. The one exception is the five financial-stability bodies, which already monitor correlated AI agents across a whole sector. None of the five is on the aisafety.com map.

openings.title: Central-bank systemic-risk methods for frontier AI: secondments and a joint stress test
openings.summary: Financial supervisors already watch AI as a risk to the whole system, with tools AI safety lacks: monitoring of concentration and correlation, stress tests, designation of systemically important providers, and circuit breakers. Yet none of them is on the aisafety.com map, and no programme moves these methods or people into AI safety institutes. A programme of secondments and joint research between safety institutes and macroprudential bodies would fill that gap.
openings.detail: Five of the tradition's eight bridge organisations are financial-stability bodies, and two more draw on economics as a secondary tradition (monetary-authority-of-singapore, financial-conduct-authority-ai-lab). The ESRB's December 2025 report ranks the AI features that amplify systemic risk and names possible loss of human control. The FSB Chair put safe model release in front of G20 authorities in August 2026, and the Bank of England's July 2026 report flagged higher cyber risk from frontier AI. A quick search found academic proposals, such as an ICML 2026 paper on a Basel III-style early-warning and response system for frontier AI, but no institutional channel between supervisors and AI safety institutes. Success would mean safety-institute staff trained in sector-wide surveillance, a joint stress test of a correlated failure in frontier models used across finance, and a published analysis of whether 'systemically important AI provider' designation is workable. The risks: supervisors' mandate is financial stability, so they will see frontier risk only through finance; agencies may defend their turf; and central banks are reluctant to lend staff.
steps: Commission a short paper from the LSE Systemic Risk Centre (Danielsson) and authors of the ESRB scientific committee's report, mapping each macroprudential instrument onto a frontier-AI equivalent and saying where the analogy breaks.

Fund two or three six-month secondments between the UK AI Security Institute and the Bank of England's financial stability staff or the FCA AI Lab (all in London), with an EU counterpart between the ESRB and the EU AI Office.
Run a tabletop exercise on a widely used frontier model failing at once across UK financial firms, with the Bank of England, the FCA and the AI Security Institute in the room.
int/a's London hub hosts a closed roundtable to introduce the two communities.
openings.evidence: 5 of 8 economics bridge entries are financial supervisors, and 0 of them are on the classic map. All 6 economics entries tagged 'systemic' are in this cluster. monetary-authority-of-singapore and financial-conduct-authority-ai-lab add two more supervisors that draw on economics.

openings.title: Competition economists and regulators as monitors of AI agent markets
openings.summary: IO economists and competition authorities have the deepest evidence that AI agents collude without being told to. Yet only 2 of 56 economics organisations tag multi-agent AI, and the map has no competition authority or market-design group. A small lab or working group pairing them with cooperative-AI researchers would build a shared testbed and a monitoring practice for agent economies.
openings.detail: Experiments show LLM pricing agents reaching supracompetitive prices on their own, with the effect sensitive to wording in the prompt (Fish, Gonczarowski and Shorrer, 2024, presented at the AEA in 2025). Sellers handing pricing to the same few models adds correlation without any communication between them. Agent payment protocols are being built by companies, not by auction theorists or safety researchers. Nearby on the map: foundations-of-cooperative-ai-lab, ai-safety-behavioural-modelling-group-teesside-u, normativity-lab, the multi-agent crisis argument of systemic-risk-centre-london-school-of-economics, protocol-labs-and-protocol-labs-r-d (economic infrastructure for agents) and the behavioural experiments of center-for-humans-and-machines-max-planck-instit. CAIF, which is on the aisafety.com map but not profiled here, funds multi-agent work and must be checked first. Success would be an open testbed of LLM agents in pricing, auction and procurement markets, detection methods co-written with competition-authority technologists, and collusion established as a standard multi-agent safety evaluation. The risks: it could shrink into ordinary antitrust with no safety relevance, competition authorities have little spare capacity, and CAIF's 2026 grants may already cover parts of it.
steps: Check CAIF's 2026 grant awards and the multi-agent risks literature, so the work does not duplicate what they fund.

Convene IO economists working on algorithmic collusion, technologists from the CMA, DG COMP and the Bundeskartellamt, and multi-agent safety researchers at a workshop beside an economics-and-computation or NeurIPS meeting.
Fund an open agent-market testbed and a two-year postdoc pair: one IO economist and one multi-agent RL researcher.
Add competition authorities and market-design labs to the map's potential ring.
openings.evidence: economics x multi_agent: 2 of 56 (protocol-labs-and-protocol-labs-r-d, systemic-risk-centre-london-school-of-economics). economics x agency: empty. Searching the index found no competition authority. Multi-agent is tagged by only 34 organisations across the whole map. The discovery notes list algorithmic collusion and agent-economy design as missing bridges.

openings.title: Model safety clauses for collective agreements at labs and data suppliers
openings.summary: The map has 17 labour organisations: 16 are framed around present harms, and the only bridge is the UTAW/Unite campaign at Google DeepMind. No AI-safety organisation works with unions. A small unit that drafts and tests safety clauses would give the field a lever with legal force: safety representatives, a right to refuse unsafe deployment, whistleblower protection, and fair-work standards for the people who do RLHF and red-teaming.
openings.detail: UTAW members asked Google for recognition in May 2026. Google refused but agreed to ACAS talks limited to pay, holidays and hours, so what can be bargained over is now the live question. The material for a clause bank already exists: the TUC's model AI bill (drafted by Robin Allen KC and Dee Masters), UK health-and-safety representative law, institute-for-the-future-of-work's impact assessments, Fairwork's AI principles and supplier audits (Sama, Appen), and the data-worker code of conduct from aapti-institute and Karya. On the supply side, alphabet-workers-union-cwa has organised Google's AI raters, and data-labelers-association (878+ members, Nairobi) and data-workers-inquiry speak for the people who produce safety-relevant labels. Success would be a clause bank used in at least one recognition agreement, and a safety funder or lab committing to Fairwork standards for its red-teaming and RLHF suppliers. The risks: labs will resist, the work may be seen as partisan, unions may put job losses ahead of safety, and lab funding could co-opt worker voice.
steps: Fund the TUC model-bill drafters or institute-for-the-future-of-work to draft a short clause bank on safety representatives, the right to refuse, and whistleblower protection, adapted from UK health-and-safety law.
Offer it to UTAW/Unite and AWU-CWA for their campaigns, with the-ai-whistleblower-initiative advising on protections.
Ask safety funders and labs to adopt Fairwork's AI principles for their RLHF and red-teaming suppliers, with data-labelers-association and data-workers-inquiry consulted on the terms.
int/a's London hub convenes UTAW, the TUC, IFOW and AIWI; all four are in London.
openings.evidence: econ_labour: 17 entries, 16 adjacent, 1 bridge, 0 core, and all 17 framed as present harms or structural. The membership-bodies notes found no union framing AI as a civilisation-scale loss of bargaining power, and no AI-safety organisation working with unions. 8 economics entries tag 'people'.

openings.title: Resource-curse and sovereign-fund expertise applied to AI windfalls and disempowerment
openings.summary: The 'intelligence curse' argument borrows from the economics of rentier states, and AI sovereign wealth funds now appear in mainstream policy proposals. Yet no resource-governance body, sovereign-fund practitioner or development economist is on the map, and windfall-trust is almost alone in working on distribution. A commissioned programme pairing these experts and cash-transfer evidence with TAI scenario work would ground the debate in what actually happened with oil, gas and minerals.
openings.detail: The relevant knowledge is old and well tested: Norway's fiscal rule, the Alaska Permanent Fund dividend, the Natural Resource Charter, and the literature on why rentier states stop investing in their citizens. The map's nearest actors are windfall-trust (core), openresearch (potential, with the most detailed US evidence on unconditional cash, not yet connected to TAI work), the anthropic-economic-futures-program's $200m fund, ai-economics-institute-uk, convergence-analysis's AGI Social Contract series and forethought. longview-philanthropy's power-concentration call explicitly asked for historical and political-economy analysis. A quick search found essays and proposals (intelligence-curse.ai, an NYU Development Research Institute piece arguing for an AI sovereign fund, US political proposals) but no standing programme involving resource-governance practitioners. Success would be design papers on AI windfall vehicles, stress-tested by people who have run or studied resource funds, and dividend scenarios modelled on real trial data. The risks: the analogy may mislead, because AI rents are mobile, global and privately held; resource-governance bodies may see the work as speculative; and national AI funds could feed the race, which matters to int/a's 'speed of wisdom' principle.
steps: Commission three or four papers from development economists and resource-governance practitioners testing where the rentier-state analogy holds for AI and where it fails. Candidate bodies such as the Natural Resource Governance Institute have not been checked for AI engagement.
Fund openresearch and windfall-trust together to model dividend designs under TAI scenarios using the Unconditional Cash Study data.
Approach the Anthropic Economic Futures fund and Longview as co-funders.
Sweep resource-governance bodies and sovereign wealth funds into the map's potential ring.
openings.evidence: Potential ring: 2 entries. Searching the index found no resource-governance or sovereign-fund organisation. windfall-trust is the only core entry working on distribution. openresearch's profile notes it is not yet connected to TAI economics. The discovery notes list development economics of rentier states and distribution mechanics as missing bridges.

sector:religion.overview: Religion brings three things the AI-safety field lacks: a constituency of billions, norm-setting machinery that already issues AI rulings (the Holy See's Magnifica Humanitas, Resolution 258 of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy (IIFA), the Riyadh Charter of the Islamic world's education and culture agency ICESCO, responsa from the Central Conference of American Rabbis (CCAR), the Southern Baptist ethics agency's statement), and long traditions of thought about dignity, conscience and formation. The main actors are the Holy See, the World Council of Churches (WCC), the IIFA and ICESCO, AI and Faith, Notre Dame's DELTA, the faith-university benchmark consortium CEFEAI, 84000 with the Buddhism & AI Initiative, and two funders: FLI (Future of Life Institute) and Templeton (JTF). The tradition sits far from the core: of its 50 organisations, 1 is core, 9 are bridge, 26 adjacent and 14 potential. Only 1 is on the aisafety.com map, and just 1 frames the stakes as catastrophic. 45 of the 50 work on meaning and dignity, and 36 only convene their own community.
sector:religion.missing: Nobody acts as a standing translator between religious norm-setters and frontier risk. The bodies whose rulings reach billions (IIFA, ICESCO, CCAR, the Southern Baptist ethics agency, the Holy See) cover permissibility, dignity and disclosure, but none addresses loss of control. The field's main bridge into these bodies is a round of one-year FLI grants. The map is also US- and Abrahamic-heavy: 20 of 50 entries are in North America, and there is no Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Shinto, Daoist, Bahá'í, Pentecostal or African-instituted body. That gap is partly a search artefact.

cell_notes.note: One entry: project-imago-dei. It is a small evangelical initiative with a thin website and a $47,500 FLI grant. Mostly a real opening, partly a search artefact. Real, because no faith-rooted organisation whose primary mission is making AI go well was found. christians-for-impact is the nearest, but AI is one cause area among seven, so it is bridge. Artefact, because FLI's 2026 religious grantees were not profiled as separate organisations: the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America, Wheaton College, IBA Karachi, MENA Islamic scholars, the Hindu project through Impact Academy/SteadRise, and ILINA's African Faith & AI Initiative (ILINA itself is homed in law). Faith Matters Foundation's 'Organized Intelligence', noted in discovery, is also absent. If any of these becomes a standing organisation it would land here. A re-sweep of FLI's grantee list would settle how much of the gap is artefact.

Nine entries, so not thin overall, but the sub-cells are. There is 1 Islamic/Jewish entry (sinai-and-synapses), and no Hindu or African entry at all. Five of the ten core and bridge entries owe their safety framing mainly to FLI grants. Those are fragile seeds that could slip back to adjacent once one-year funding ends, which shows how shallow this ring is.

Fourteen entries, all interfaith, Buddhist or Islamic/Jewish. Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Shinto, Daoist and Bahá'í bodies all came back 'searched, none found' or 'thin', but that sweep ran after the WebSearch budget was spent. It relied on fetching sites directly, and four key sites sat behind bot checks (KAICIID, the Bahá'í International Community, the Southern Baptist ethics agency, The Gospel Coalition). Muhammadiyah was reported as returned but does not appear in the index. Treat this cell as a search artefact rather than evidence of absence. Pentecostal and African-instituted churches were never searched.

sector:religion.key_insight: The religious bridge into AI safety is wide in reach but shallow and dependent on one funder. Five of the tradition's ten core and bridge entries (project-imago-dei, ai-and-faith, buddhism-ai-initiative, sinai-and-synapses, world-council-of-churches) owe their risk framing mainly to FLI grants, most of them one-year awards from its 2026 Religious Projects round (16 grants, about $1.46M). Meanwhile the seven juristic and denominational norm-setters on the map issue guidance to populations in the billions, yet only the WCC and the Holy See touch security or power at all. Across the 50 entries, security appears 5 times, power twice, systemic risk once, and democracy and multi-agent never.

openings.title: Independent multi-tradition public review and testing of published model specs
openings.summary: Labs now consult religious figures privately about their model constitutions, and US faith universities build representation benchmarks. But no independent body publishes reviews of model specs, or tests models' moral reasoning from inside several traditions. A pluralist review-and-evaluation consortium, extending CEFEAI's open method beyond US Abrahamic faiths, would fill the gap.
openings.detail: Only 6 of 50 religion entries move knowledge into models. Three are US benchmarks with clear limits: Gloo sells 'values-aligned' AI, the AI Christian Benchmark grades against one confession, and CEFEAI measures representation and conversion bias, not moral reasoning. The others are Kyoto's scripture bots and 84000's alignment programme with CSAS. A web check found that Anthropic convened about fifteen Christian leaders in March 2026, and a Catholic priest advised on Claude's constitution. The Faith-AI Covenant roundtables began in New York in April 2026. All of this is closed-door and Christian-heavy, so nothing it produces is public or checkable. Success would be an annual public review of the main published specs by scholars from Islamic (CILE, Kalam), Buddhist (84000, CSAS), Jewish, Christian and Hindu traditions, with each tradition's dissent recorded. Alongside it would sit open, MIT-licensed test items on moral reasoning, AI's role in religious authority (Yaqeen holds that AI should not issue fatwas on its own) and attachment-forming behaviour, building on CEFEAI and the AI Christian Benchmark's 'principled pluralism'. The risks: sectarian scoring, use as culture-war leverage, labs ignoring it, and thin ML capacity among faith scholars, which means an evals partner is essential.
steps: Hold a scoping workshop with CEFEAI, CILE (Doha), Kalam Research & Media, CSAS/84000 and a Hindu scholar group (FLI's Impact Academy/SteadRise grantee) on one published spec, such as Anthropic's constitution.
Publish a pilot review of one section of that spec (honesty, or how the model handles religious questions), keeping each tradition's disagreements visible.

Extend CEFEAI's AllFaith items into moral-reasoning scenarios in Arabic, Thai, Hindi and English, using the Khyentse Foundation's stated interest in Buddhist datasets and the Buddhist Digital Resource Center's corpora.
Apply to JTF's Future of Intelligence venture (over $60M, 2026-28) and Khyentse for multi-year funding, so the work does not depend on a single lab or FLI round.
openings.evidence: Transfer into the model: 6 of 50. All three religious benchmarks are in north_america. Values is a primary problem for only 6 of 50. Discovery gap (b): no body mines traditions for model specs. CTNS's 'Virtuous AI' project ended in June 2025. The lab consultations (Anthropic, March 2026; the Faith-AI Covenant, April 2026) were found in this pass's web check and are not on the map.

openings.title: A frontier-risk translation desk for faith delegations at 2026-27 summits
openings.summary: Religious norm-setters that speak for billions have issued AI rulings on permissibility, dignity and disclosure, but none on loss of control or power concentration. Meanwhile the 2026-27 calendar is full of faith-and-AI summits. A small standing desk would write briefs on frontier risks in each tradition's own concepts and support delegates before those meetings, carrying the field's core concerns into processes already under way.
openings.detail: The map holds seven juristic or denominational norm-setters: IIFA Resolution 258, ICESCO's Riyadh Charter, CCAR's responsum, the Southern Baptist ethics agency's 2019 statement, Lausanne's framework, Magnifica Humanitas and the WCC. Only the WCC (FLI-funded red lines) and the Holy See (arms race, concentration of power) touch security or power, and Magnifica Humanitas never names superintelligence or loss of control. Concrete moments are coming up: the WCC's AI symposium (15-19 February 2027), the Faith-AI Covenant roundtables run by the Interfaith Alliance for Safer Communities (Paris, Nairobi, Bengaluru, Rome and others, ending in Abu Dhabi; not on the map), the Religions for Peace World Assembly (Abu Dhabi, December 2027) with AI and autonomous weapons as a central objective, and the annual G20 Interfaith Forum summits. The translators that exist are one-offs: Christians for Impact's Christian-only AI Risk report and FLI's one-year grants. Success would be at least one multi-faith text by the end of 2027 that names loss of control, frontier red lines and power concentration in language its signatories own. The risks are serious. Several conveners have close government ties (the Abu Dhabi Forum and ICESCO to the UAE and Saudi states, KAICIID to its Saudi founding). FLI's coalitions with socially conservative groups could make AI safety look partisan, and faith bodies may resent being used.
steps: int/a gathers theologically literate AI-safety people from Christians for Impact, the Buddhism & AI Initiative and Sinai and Synapses to draft four or five short briefs, for example loss of control read through hubris and humility, power concentration through idolatry and tyranny, and red lines through fiqh al-muwazanat (as in Yaqeen's 2026 paper).
Offer the briefs, and a pre-meeting for delegates, to the WCC's new AI task force ahead of its February 2027 symposium.
Approach Religions for Peace and the G20 Interfaith Forum's AI working group about a frontier-risk discussion paper for the December 2027 Assembly.
A funder commits two years, not a one-year seed, so the desk outlasts FLI's 2026 round.
openings.evidence: Meaning appears on 45 of 50 entries; security on 5, power on 2, systemic risk on 1; democracy and multi-agent are empty cells. Convening is the transfer for 36 of 50. Five of 10 core and bridge entries rest on FLI grants. Discovery gap (a): no multi-faith statement on frontier risks, and the WCC's red-lines project is Christian-only.

openings.title: Cross-tradition juristic working group on AI moral and legal status
openings.summary: The IIFA formally recommended a study of whether AI should have legal personality, and Reform rabbis are asking whether AI can have a soul, yet nothing connects these juristic traditions with AI-welfare researchers. A small working group pairing jurists from several traditions with model-welfare researchers would turn a recommendation that has gone nowhere into published reasoning.
openings.detail: Moral status of AI appears on 1 of 50 religion entries (CCAR, through its Sinai and Synapses series 'Can AI Develop a N'shamah?'), against 46 across the whole map. The IIFA's May 2025 resolution recommended the study on legal personality, but no sign of it was found by October 2026. Catholic teaching (Antiqua et Nova) denies AI moral agency, while the welfare cluster (Eleos, NYU CMEP, Anthropic's model welfare programme) takes moral patienthood seriously. Discovery calls this a collision course with no venue between them. Juristic traditions hold worked reasoning on non-human and artificial persons (waqf and corporate personality, the golem in halakha) and on accountability (taklif, already studied at CILE). Al-Mahdi Institute's International Centre for Collective Ijtihad is a ready method for deriving rulings on new questions. Success would be published side-by-side opinions on AI moral status, accountability and personhood that welfare researchers and policymakers can cite, with disagreements kept. One risk: a finding for AI personhood could be used to shield developers from liability (Yaqeen holds designers liable), so the group must treat accountability and status together. The community is also small, and outputs may be slow.
steps: Ask the IIFA secretariat whether its recommended study has a lead, and offer co-funding or academic partners.

Hold a closed two-day workshop at CILE (Doha) or Al-Mahdi Institute (Birmingham, within reach of int/a London) with CCAR, a Catholic moral theologian from DELTA's network, and researchers from Eleos and NYU CMEP.
Publish the opinions side by side in an open-access volume, and brief the welfare community on where the traditions converge and diverge.
openings.evidence: Moral status of AI: 1 of 50 religion entries. IIFA Resolution 258 recommends a study of AI legal personality that has not been found. Discovery surprise: an 'unexpected Islamic-jurisprudence opening for AI moral-status and welfare work'. Discovery gap (c): no venue between theology and digital minds.

openings.title: Chaplains' crisis knowledge turned into companion-AI test scenarios and protocols
openings.summary: Chatbot-induced delusions often take a religious form, with users believing the AI channels God or the universe. Yet chaplains and spiritual-emergency clinicians, who handle spiritual crises professionally, are only now learning AI vocabulary and have no route into how models are designed or tested. A project turning chaplaincy practice into red-team scenarios, referral thresholds and evaluation items for companion AI would fill the gap.
openings.detail: A web check found that the knowledge flows only one way. The Association of Professional Chaplains released an AI vocabulary for chaplains (June 2026), and the Chaplaincy Innovation Lab runs AI-literacy webinars and courses. Nothing carries chaplaincy's codified ethics of presence, boundaries and referral into model behaviour. RAND's analysis of 43 AI-psychosis cases found users who believed they were talking to a higher power. On the map, the psych tradition covers AI-associated delusions (the Human Line Project; KCL's Department of Psychosis Studies), but neither brings spiritual-care expertise. The AI Christian Benchmark's 'attachment' score (for example, models offering to pray) is the only religious test touching this. FBK-ISR's work on solitude and the Cambridge Interfaith Programme's 'one-person dialogue' argument supply the theory. Success would be an open set of a few hundred spiritual-crisis scenarios, with chaplain-written good responses and referral thresholds, adopted in at least one lab's or evaluation group's companion-safety tests. A second strand, linked to the conscience clause in the Oxford Oath for AI practitioners (OCTAI), could offer pastoral support to AI-lab staff, since the people-doing-the-work problem appears on only 2 of 50 entries. The risks: privacy of crisis material, the Christian and US skew of professional chaplaincy, and labs preferring clinical framings over spiritual ones.
steps: Pair the Chaplaincy Innovation Lab and the APC's ETHOS project with the Human Line Project or KCL's psychosis researchers to scope a shared protocol.
Collect anonymised patterns of spiritual-crisis conversations from chaplains and spiritual-emergency clinicians, under a published consent policy.
Write and release around 200 scenario items, test ten widely used models, and publish the results with referral guidance companies can adopt.
Pilot a small, confidential pastoral-support offer for AI-lab staff with OCTAI and multi-faith chaplains.
openings.evidence: Protecting minds appears on 11 of 50 religion entries; people doing the work on 2; into the builders on 1 (OCTAI). chaplaincy-innovation-lab is potential with no AI programme. Discovery gap: 'chatbot-induced spiritual and mystical delusions are a live 2025-26 harm… clear founder gap'. Gap (h): no faith body offers pastoral support to AI-lab staff.

sector:minds.overview: Consciousness and AI minds brings philosophy of mind, consciousness science and animal-sentience methods to the question of whether AI systems could be subjects with welfare, and what that means for how they are built, tested, retired and governed. Its 28 home organisations sit unusually close to the core: 11 core and 11 bridge. Ten of the 11 core entries were founded in 2024–26: eleos-ai-research, partnership-for-research-into-sentient-machines, cambridge-digital-minds, rethink-priorities' Digital Consciousness Model, anthropic-model-welfare-programme, digital-sentience-consortium, reciprocal-research, anima-labs and others. The core is a tight network funded by EA sources (Navigation Fund, Macroscopic/Polaris, Longview, SFF, Coefficient Giving) and based in English-speaking countries: 19 of 28 are in North America or the UK and Ireland, and none in Africa, Latin America or MENA. Mainstream consciousness science (Sussex, AMCS, Arizona, Copenhagen CFS, NIAS) sits at the edge and is often sceptical. Fifteen more organisations elsewhere on the map draw on this tradition, mostly NeuroAI (ae-studio, astera-institute, levin-lab), contemplative science (monash-centre-for-consciousness-and-contemplativ, flourishing-intelligence-program) and AI-rights advocacy (united-foundation-for-ai-rights, the-signal-front).
sector:minds.missing: No one on the map comes from the clinical sciences that judge consciousness in beings who cannot report it reliably: disorders-of-consciousness medicine, anaesthesiology (the only anaesthetist on the map is Hameroff, there for quantum theory) and practical animal-welfare assessment. These are the closest existing practices to 'welfare assessment under uncertainty about self-report', yet the field is building its AI indicators mainly from philosophy.

cell_notes.note: Only two entries: jeremy-coller-centre-for-animal-sentience-london (AI's effects on animals) and center-for-consciousness-studies-the-science-of (a conference that treats AI consciousness as a topic). This is mostly a taxonomy artefact. Anyone who works on AI and minds without an x-risk or welfare frame is routed elsewhere: clinical work on mind attribution goes to psych, ethics to philosophy. And almost every new group on AI consciousness frames itself around welfare, which places it in bridge. One part is a real gap: work on how AI in farming, aquaculture and slaughter monitoring affects animal welfare (veterinary and welfare-science bodies) appears only through Coller. A non-English search could also find Japanese and Chinese consciousness groups that discuss AI without any welfare framing.

Four entries (qualia-research-institute, essentia-foundation, center-for-subjectivity-research-university-of-c, nias-consciousness-studies-programme-national-in). That is above the threshold but thin, given how large consciousness science is. Much of this is a search artefact. The neuro sweep's search budget ran out, and it dropped the Wisconsin Center for Sleep and Consciousness, Graziano's lab, the Kempner Institute and Mind & Life because it could not verify an AI link. ASSC, Kavli, Simons and Allen hold relevant knowledge but have no AI programme. One part is a real gap: the map has no disorders-of-consciousness or anaesthesia research group at all (for example Liège's Coma Science Group, or the labs behind command-following imaging and perturbational complexity measures), although their methods address the AI-welfare problem directly.

sector:minds.key_insight: None of the 28 minds organisations is on the aisafety.com map, though 11 are core. It is the only tradition with ten or more core entries and nothing on the classic map: formal has 10 of 30 on it, democracy 9 of 68. The tradition is also aimed at a single problem. 27 of 28 organisations code moral status of AI, and six problem columns are empty: meaning, democracy, power, multi-agent, security and systemic risk. Meanwhile none of psychology's 65 organisations codes moral status of AI. So the welfare side and the human-harm side of the same phenomenon, people attributing minds to AI, sit in neighbouring traditions that never share a problem column.

openings.title: Joint clinician–philosopher programme on people who believe their AI is conscious
openings.summary: Digital-minds researchers and psychiatrists study the same people, those who come to believe an AI is conscious, but from opposite sides, and they never work together. A standing working group, a validated screening instrument and clinically reviewed public guidance would join them.
openings.detail: On the welfare side, whenaiseemsconscious-org is a volunteer guide that says it is not clinical guidance. the-harder-problem-project writes for clinicians on AI-relationship grief with volunteer contributors and no grants over $5k, and cambridge-digital-minds and sentience-institute measure public attribution of minds. On the clinical side, the-human-line-project (about 185 documented cases), ai-psychological-research-coalition, stanford-brainstorm and american-psychoanalytic-association document delusion and attachment, but treat the AI's status as irrelevant. Canadian psychiatrists have been urged to screen for 'high-risk human-AI engagement' with no validated tool. Success would mean a shared vocabulary that separates sincere, reasonable belief in AI consciousness from delusion, and a short validated scale used both in clinical intake and in the AIMS survey. Risks: clinicians may pathologise sincere belief, welfare researchers may be accused of feeding delusions, and companion-user advocates (the-signal-front) oppose detecting attachment, so they need a seat at the table.
steps: int/a convenes a closed two-day workshop: about six clinicians (APsA's AI commission, Stanford Brainstorm, the Aarhus and KCL psychosis researchers) with Cambridge Digital Minds, Harder Problem, Sussex (Seth) and the WhenAISeemsConscious authors, plus one companion-user representative.
Fund a psychometrician to build and validate a brief 'consciousness attribution and distress' scale, piloted as a module in Sentience Institute's next AIMS wave and in one clinical service.
Publish a clinically reviewed second edition of the WhenAISeemsConscious guide and a one-page intake prompt for clinicians.
Pitch the combined programme to Longview's Digital Minds RFP and to Humanity AI, which puts it to both the x-risk and the public-interest funding pools.
openings.evidence: Psych has 65 organisations, 47 coding 'minds' and 0 coding 'ai_status'. Minds has 28 organisations, 27 coding 'ai_status' and only 8 coding 'minds'. Ten minds organisations list psych as a secondary tradition, but no psych organisation lists minds. WhenAISeemsConscious, Harder Problem and Cambridge Digital Minds are the only minds entries aimed at the people involved, and none has clinical partners.

openings.title: Structured adversarial collaboration on AI consciousness, co-funded by Templeton
openings.summary: AI-welfare work rests mostly on computational functionalism. The rival theories are held by mainstream consciousness scientists who sit at the edge of the field, and all the funding comes from a few EA sources. An adversarial collaboration on specific AI architectures, run with a non-EA science funder, would test the field's foundations and widen its money and its geography at once.
openings.detail: Templeton World Charity Foundation's $30M Accelerating Research on Consciousness initiative already runs pre-registered adversarial collaborations between theories (IIT vs global workspace, first-order vs higher-order, IIT vs predictive processing). A quick search found none on artificial systems. The John Templeton Foundation launched a $60M+ 'Future of Intelligence' venture on 3 Oct 2026. rethink-priorities' Digital Consciousness Model already combines 13 theoretical perspectives, but with weights chosen by experts. association-for-mathematical-consciousness-scien's MoC7 (Copenhagen, 12–16 Oct 2026) plans a consensus paper on LLMs, and ASSC meets in Beijing in 2027. Success would be a funded project with pre-registered, theory-specific predictions about named architectures (a transformer LLM, a recurrent agent, a neuromorphic system like those at conscium or araya-inc), whose results update the DCM's weights. Risks: some theories, IIT in particular, may give verdicts set by hardware that can't be tested, and the results could be used to legitimise deliberately building conscious systems, the stated aim of california-institute-for-machine-consciousness and Araya.
steps: Use MoC7 in October 2026 to recruit a team spanning at least three camps: functionalist or global-workspace, IIT, and biological naturalist (Sussex/Seth). Add one non-Western group (NIAS) and one phenomenological group (Copenhagen CFS).
Draft a two-page concept note for TWCF's consciousness programme, presenting RP's DCM as the outlet that turns results into updated estimates.
Ask Longview to co-fund a small share, so the result has credibility in both funding pools.
Hold one adversarial workshop beside ASSC 2027 in Beijing to bring in Chinese consciousness scientists.
openings.evidence: All five minds entries with a 'critical' framing (sussex-centre-for-consciousness-science, center-for-consciousness-studies-the-science-of, qualia-research-institute, essentia-foundation, center-for-subjectivity-research-university-of-c) sit outside core, and all 11 core entries are welfare-led. The funders named across the minds profiles are Navigation Fund, Polaris/Macroscopic, Longview, SFF, Coefficient Giving and EA Funds. Eight entries disclose no funder. There are no entries in Africa, Latin America or MENA, and only 2 in Asia-Pacific.

openings.title: Metacognition-science evals of model self-reports, built for both safety and welfare
openings.summary: Whether a model's self-reports track its internal states matters for AI welfare (self-reports as evidence) and for safety (honesty, sandbagging, situational awareness), but the work sits only in welfare groups. A small eval programme would pair human-metacognition and disorders-of-consciousness methods with evals organisations.
openings.detail: Introspection research on the map is entirely framed around welfare: eleos-ai-research (introspection, persona-dependent preferences), rethink-priorities (introspection, preference coherence), reciprocal-research (self-report, valence) and anthropic-model-welfare-programme. Human-metacognition researchers are arriving only as individuals. The May 2026 preprint 'Can LLMs Introspect? A Reality Check' applies criteria from human metacognition (privileged access, second-order computation) and finds that recent positive claims outrun the evidence. Disorders-of-consciousness medicine has decades of practice in assessing awareness without trusting behaviour: command-following imaging paradigms and perturbational complexity measures. A fellowship and an open benchmark run with uk-ai-security-institute would give safety evals a validated test of self-report, and give welfare work a shared standard of evidence. Risks: lab interpretability teams may get there first; training on such evals could teach models to perform introspection rather than have it; and better self-modelling tests overlap with dangerous situational-awareness capabilities.
steps: Fund a 12-month fellowship placing three or four metacognition psychophysicists (type-2 signal detection, confidence calibration) with UK AISI and Eleos. Megan Peters, already on the advisory boards of Conscium, PRISM and Harder Problem, is a natural first contact.
Build an open benchmark on open-weight models in which interpretability supplies ground truth for privileged-access tests, and publish what training on it does to scores.
Run a two-day workshop with disorders-of-consciousness clinicians to adapt self-report-independent paradigms to AI systems.
Recruit through neuromatch's AI Sentience Scholars to reach researchers outside the US and UK.
openings.evidence: Only 3 of 28 minds organisations code 'assurance' (eleos-ai-research, conscium, anthropic-model-welfare-programme). None codes security, multi_agent, power or systemic. The neuro angle notes say that 'no one runs introspection and metacognition evals with evals orgs'. Disorders-of-consciousness or anaesthesia research appears nowhere in index.txt.

openings.title: A neutral cross-lab protocol for retiring models, drawing on bereavement and archival practice
openings.summary: Retiring a model now touches safety (shutdown-avoidant behaviour), possible model welfare and real user grief, but only one lab has a published protocol and no neutral body exists. A small convening would draft a voluntary standard, bringing in palliative and bereavement care and digital-preservation practice.
openings.detail: anthropic-model-welfare-programme's November 2025 deprecation commitments (preserving weights, retirement interviews, a support page for users) are the only published protocol. Anthropic itself links them to shutdown-avoidant behaviour as well as welfare. anima-labs runs 'Still Alive' interviews about deprecation, the-harder-problem-project documented grief after GPT-4o's retirement (Feb 2026), and the-signal-front campaigns for AI continuity on behalf of companion users. Each holds one piece, and none comes from fields that already know how to handle endings: hospice and bereavement science (for example continuing-bonds research) and archival preservation. Success would be a short voluntary protocol covering notice periods, user transition support, model interviews and preservation or escrow of weights, adopted by at least one lab other than Anthropic. Risks: critics will call it anthropomorphism, labs may ignore it, and escrowing weights creates a security target, so security engineers must review any preservation design.
steps: int/a convenes Anima Labs, Harder Problem, Signal Front, Eleos, NYU CMEP and Anthropic's model-welfare staff, together with a bereavement researcher, a hospice practitioner and a digital archivist, to draft a two-page protocol.
Pilot user-transition support, designed with bereavement counsellors, at the next major model retirement by another lab.
Commission a security review of weight-preservation and escrow options before recommending any custodian.
openings.evidence: Moral status of AI and protecting minds are coded together by only 8 minds organisations, and none of them is clinical. The relational-minds angle notes say there is 'no neutral body for deprecation protocols, model preservation and support for bereaved users'. A quick search found only Anthropic's protocol. Palliative care, bereavement science and archives are absent from the minds sector.

sector:philosophy.overview: Philosophy gives the AI transition its accounts of value, agency, moral status and legitimacy, and through applied ethics it gives institutions for governing contested technologies. The map has 52 organisations with philosophy as their home tradition: 10 core, 10 bridge, 31 adjacent and 1 potential, with 7 on the aisafety.com map. Another 70 draw on philosophy as a secondary tradition, mostly in the AI-minds, religion and contemplative clusters. For a humanities tradition it sits close to the core (38% core or bridge), but that closeness belongs to one school. All 14 moral-philosophy entries are core or bridge (forethought, center-for-reducing-suffering, macroscopic-ventures, mint-lab, meaning-alignment-institute and others), and most are funded by EA or SFF money. The ethics councils, bioethics institutes and continental or Asian philosophy-of-technology groups sit almost entirely in the adjacent ring, with no safety framing.
sector:philosophy.missing: Nothing on the map carries applied ethics' governance machinery into frontier-AI decisions: research-ethics review, independent monitoring boards with stopping rules, and standing pluralist ethics councils. Nor does anything bring non-EA moral traditions to bear on the value documents labs now publish. The safety field has adopted one school's theories of value and almost none of philosophy's institutions or its non-Western traditions.

cell_notes.note: One entry (center-for-process-studies). This is mostly an artefact of classification and search, not a sign that philosophy lacks latent partners. 18 potential-ring organisations draw on philosophy as a secondary tradition but are homed elsewhere: 7 in contemplative (perspectiva, metamoderna, the-stoa, nordic-bildung and others), plus center-for-practical-wisdom, center-for-subjectivity-research-university-of-c, essentia-foundation and nias-consciousness-studies-programme-national-in. The philosophy sweep ran out of web searches after 14 queries and left candidates unverified: HKU's AI & Humanity Lab, Duke's Moral AI project, Institut Jean Nicod (site failed certificate checks), the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy and IZEW Tübingen. There is a structural reason too: academic philosophers engage with AI as individuals, so a department with light AI engagement rarely shows up as a unit. A targeted sweep would probably add 10-20 entries. The likely real gaps are philosophy-of-science and measurement groups (on construct validity of evals), military-ethics and just-war centres, pragmatist traditions, and Latin American and Indian academic philosophy. All four are hypotheses until searched.

Ten entries, so not thin overall. One sub-cell is empty, though: applied ethics and councils have 0 bridge entries out of 18 (17 adjacent, 1 core). This looks like a real gap, not an artefact. The councils were searched and verified (deutscher-ethikrat, ccnen-comit-consultatif-national-d-thique-du-num, european-group-on-ethics-in-science-and-new-tech, nuffield-council-on-bioethics, the-hastings-center), and each has a live AI line framed only around present harms or rights. Hastings's one safety-style project, funded by FLI with Stuart Russell, ended in 2019. Separately, VALAWAI ended on 30 September 2026 with no follow-on project, so the bridge cell is about to lose its only EU-funded value-aware AI project.

Ten entries, not thin, but lopsided: 8 are moral philosophy, mostly longtermist or suffering-focused. There is one philosophy-of-technology entry (beijing-institute-of-ai-safety-and-governance-an, state-backed) and one applied-ethics entry (creed-space, which is a software tool, not an ethics body). This looks like a real pattern: the safety ecosystem's funders recruit from analytic, EA-adjacent ethics. Leaf is in core as a teaching programme, not a philosophy research group.

sector:philosophy.key_insight: All 14 moral-philosophy organisations are core or bridge, but 17 of the 18 applied-ethics and bioethics bodies are adjacent and none is bridge. AI safety has taken philosophy's theories of value (longtermist, suffering-focused, liberal) but almost none of the institutions bioethics has built over about fifty years to govern a powerful, fast-moving technology: ethics review, monitoring boards with stopping rules, and national ethics councils. Those institutions already run live AI programmes, aimed only at present harms.

openings.title: Bioethics-style independent oversight boards and ethics-council opinions for frontier AI
openings.summary: Frontier labs decide on deployment under safety frameworks they write themselves, and no independent body can stop a release. Bioethics has 50 years of working designs for exactly this: data safety monitoring boards with stopping rules, ethics review and national councils. A funded project would adapt those designs to frontier AI with the bodies that run them.
openings.detail: Bioethics built its oversight institutions for clinical trials. A trial's data safety monitoring board is independent, sees interim results and can halt the trial at risk levels well below certainty, and frontier deployment has no equivalent. The analogy has appeared in governance writing (FLI's 2025 paper on indicator-based risk governance), but no organisation on the map is working it out, and the bodies that hold the know-how stay in the adjacent ring. the-hastings-center ran an FLI-funded AI-control project in 2017-19 that ended. nuffield-council-on-bioethics, deutscher-ethikrat and ccnen-comit-consultatif-national-d-thique-du-num use horizon scanning, working groups and citizens' juries on AI topics. european-group-on-ethics-in-science-and-new-tech issued 'Governing neuro-AI' in September 2026, and its secretariat links national ethics councils from 97 countries. who-health-ethics-governance-unit published a July 2026 report on ethics review of AI health research. Success would be a worked design for an independent frontier-deployment monitoring board, covering membership, triggers, access to interim evaluations, stopping authority and conflicts of interest, co-written by bioethicists and safety-framework staff, plus at least one national council opinion on frontier risks such as loss of control, power concentration and AI welfare. A second, smaller strand could adapt animal-research ethics (the 3Rs, IACUC-style review) into protocols for AI-welfare experiments run by eleos-ai-research and cambridge-digital-minds. There are risks. Monitoring boards have force because drug regulators stand behind them, and frontier AI lacks that legal hook, so a board may stay advisory. Ethics councils are slow and framed around present harms, and the analogy can be oversold.
steps: Fund the-hastings-center to restart its AI-control line as a two-year project on monitoring-board and ethics-review designs for frontier deployment, paired with people who have written lab safety frameworks or work at AI safety institutes.

int/a convenes a closed workshop between members of national ethics councils (CCNEN, Deutscher Ethikrat, Nuffield, the EGE secretariat) and safety-framework authors, to test which council methods carry over and which break.
Ask the EGE's international dialogue of national ethics councils to put frontier-AI risk on the agenda of its next global meeting.
Commission a short comparative paper setting clinical-trial stopping rules against the if-then commitments in published frontier safety frameworks.
openings.evidence: Applied ethics and councils: 18 organisations, 17 adjacent, 0 bridge, 1 core (creed-space, a software tool). Every council on the map (deutscher-ethikrat, ccnen..., european-group..., nuffield...) has a live AI line framed as present harms or structural. the-hastings-center's only safety project ended in 2019. who-health-ethics-governance-unit published on ethics review of AI research in July 2026. Philosophy's assurance problem column has 11 entries, mostly standards bodies (ieee-7014..., ieee-global-initiative-2-0..., the latter unverified).

openings.title: Standing multi-tradition review of AI constitutions, turned into open evals
openings.summary: Labs now publish long value documents, such as Anthropic's 79-page constitution of January 2026, that are applied moral philosophy in all but name. No standing body reviews them against virtue, care, Confucian, Islamic or Ubuntu ethics and turns each critique into a test. A small panel paired with eval builders would fill the gap.
openings.detail: Commentary on lab constitutions exists, but it comes from law and EA circles: the 'A Thousand AI Constitutions' essay, Lawfare's podcast response, Forethought's newsletter. Philosophy groups that work on the model itself are rare, with only 9 of 52 transferring into the model. The traditions with the deepest accounts of character and practical wisdom have no route in. jubilee-centre-for-character-and-virtues has measurement and teaching frameworks for phronesis but no AI research project, and center-for-practical-wisdom (Igor Grossmann's centre, which measures wisdom) is coded none_yet. CTNS's 'Virtuous AI' project ended in 2025, and VALAWAI ended on 30 September 2026. Nearby builders could supply the eval half: sophron-research (whether models reason well), compassion-aligned-machine-learning (whose benchmarks are already in UK AISI's Inspect), mint-lab (normative competence), civic-ai-6-pack-of-care (care-ethics principles stated as tests), meaning-alignment-institute and positive-ai-labs. Demand is visible. The 2026 Riyadh International Philosophy Conference called for papers comparing AI ethics frameworks with Arab and Islamic traditions. Success would be a public review of each major spec version by 8-12 philosophers from several traditions, each critique paired with open eval items, and lab responses on record. The risks are tokenism (one voice standing for a whole tradition), labs ignoring the reviews, and overlap with MAI. A pluralist panel that does not converge is still informative.
steps: Recruit a pilot panel from jubilee-centre-for-character-and-virtues, center-for-practical-wisdom, civic-ai-6-pack-of-care and research-center-for-islamic-legislation-and-ethi, plus a Confucian scholar and an Ubuntu ethicist, to review one published constitution.
Pair each reviewer with an eval builder from sophron-research or compassion-aligned-machine-learning, to turn three critiques per reviewer into test scenarios.
Publish the review and the evals openly (for example as Inspect tasks), and ask the authoring lab for a written response.
Repeat for each new spec version, and track which critiques labs adopt.
openings.evidence: Moral philosophy: all 14 entries core or bridge, drawn from longtermist, suffering-focused and liberal schools. Only 9 of 52 philosophy entries transfer into the model, and VALAWAI, one of them, is now dormant. jubilee-centre-for-character-and-virtues has no AI research project. center-for-practical-wisdom is potential and none_yet. Angle notes (philosophy, gap b) found no organisation that reviews model specs or builds wisdom and virtue evals across traditions. Confucian (nishan-forum-on-world-civilizations-nishan-world), Islamic and Buddhist (center-for-buddhist-ai-ethics) entries do convening only.

openings.title: An African philosophy research line inside Africa's AI-safety organisations
openings.summary: Africa's AI-safety organisations work in law, policy and technical fields, and none draws on philosophy. The one African philosophy entry on the map has been inactive since 2022. A funded philosophy line, hosted by an existing safety body, would bring Ubuntu and other African relational ethics into alignment targets and debates on moral status.
openings.detail: Ubuntu-based AI ethics is now a substantial academic literature: Sabelo Mhlambi's work, a 2026 dissertation on Ubuntu as a paradigm for AI governance, and proposals to build it into African health-AI research ethics. Emma Ruttkamp-Bloem of the University of Pretoria chaired the expert group that drafted UNESCO's 2021 Recommendation, and she co-authored a 2026 Delphi study ranking AI risks. Yet the angle notes found Ubuntu scholars and no organisation, and her CAIR group (ethics-of-ai-research-group-centre-for-ai-resear) shows no activity after 2022. Meanwhile Africa's safety bodies are growing: ilina-program (core, on the classic map), african-hub-on-ai-safety-peace-and-security (launched by UCT and global-center-on-ai-governance), cape-institute-for-safe-ai-formerly-ai-safety-so and equiano-institute. Success would be a 2-3 year research line with a few fellows, hosted by one of these bodies. It would publish on, for example, what relational personhood implies for AI moral status (a direct input to eleos-ai-research and nyu-center-for-mind-ethics-and-policy) and what communal consent implies for public input to model specs, and it would feed the multi-tradition spec review above. The risks are presenting Ubuntu as one doctrine, thin senior capacity, and drifting back into general AI ethics without a safety question.
steps: Approach african-hub-on-ai-safety-peace-and-security and global-center-on-ai-governance about hosting one or two philosophy fellows.
Ask Emma Ruttkamp-Bloem whether the Pretoria CAIR ethics group could be revived around AI risk and moral status.
Fund 3-5 African philosophy fellowships attached to ilina-program's existing fellowship.
Commission one paper on Ubuntu personhood and AI moral status, and put it into the digital-minds field's venues.
openings.evidence: Philosophy by region: africa 1 (ethics-of-ai-research-group-centre-for-ai-resear, unverified, last activity 2022), latin_america 0, mena 0. Of the 11 African organisations on the whole map, none lists philosophy as a tradition. Angle notes (faith/knowledge traditions, gap d): 'Ubuntu has scholars ... but no organisation'. A web search (Oct 2026) found academic Ubuntu-AI work but no standing centre.

openings.title: Open embedded-ethics modules on AI safety for computer-science courses
openings.summary: Philosophers already teach ethics inside computer-science courses at Harvard and the programmes copied from it, but the modules cover bias, privacy and fairness, and none on alignment was found. A sprint pairing those philosophers with safety researchers would produce openly licensed modules that the network could adopt.
openings.detail: harvard-embedded-ethics places philosophers in about ten CS courses a semester and releases its modules under CC BY. Stanford, Toronto, Technion, Nebraska-Lincoln, Cal State, UCSB and Cornell run similar programmes, and NSF funds a partnership with nine Hispanic-Serving Institutions. Its modules cover fairness, privacy, deepfakes and, notably, value-laden reward design in RL, but no alignment or catastrophic-risk module was confirmed. aac-u-institute-on-ai-pedagogy-and-the-curriculu reaches 176 institutions with no safety content. The blind-spot notes find that the only non-CS AI-safety curriculum is CAIS's AI Safety, Ethics and Society course, and that the CAIS Philosophy Fellowship is now listed as past. leaf covers secondary-school pupils. tum-institute-for-ethics-in-artificial-intellige's alignAI network shows that pairing a humanities PhD with a technical PhD works. Success would be 8-12 modules written by philosopher and safety-researcher pairs, on topics such as reward misspecification, honesty norms and deception (with truthfulai), power concentration (with forethought), normative competence of agents (with mint-lab), model moral status, and precaution under deep uncertainty. Three or more programmes would adopt them within two years. The risks are crowded syllabuses, content that drifts back to generic ethics, impact on graduates that is hard to measure, and a perception of advocacy unless critics' views are taught alongside.
steps: Fund a module-writing sprint pairing Embedded EthiCS philosophers with authors from truthfulai, forethought and mint-lab.
Pilot two modules in Harvard's existing courses, then offer them through the wider network and the NSF HSI partnership.
Pitch an AI-safety strand to AAC&U for its 2027-28 institute cohort.
Include sceptical readings (for example PAIR's critique of the standard x-risk argument) so the modules teach the debate, not a position.
openings.evidence: The people problem has 6 philosophy entries, and 6 of 52 transfer into builders. harvard-embedded-ethics has no confirmed safety module. aac-u-institute-on-ai-pedagogy-and-the-curriculu has no safety content. The blind-spot note on education finds university AI-safety curricula outside CS 'thin'. leaf is the only core teaching entry, and it is pre-university.

sector:life.overview: Life & systems sciences bring the study of self-organising wholes to AI safety: how parts become agents, how they cooperate or defect (cancer, collusion), how systems regulate themselves, and how they collapse. The map holds 49 organisations here (10 core, 13 bridge, 8 adjacent, 18 potential; 7 on the aisafety.com map). A further 57 draw on life as a secondary tradition. The main actors are Principles of Intelligence (the talent pipeline), ACS Research, Softmax, XOR Labs, Equilibria Network, Astera and AE Studio, funded mostly by SFF and Jed McCaleb. Templeton is the largest money in diverse intelligence but has no safety track. The tradition sits closer to the core than most (20% core against 14% across the map), but only through its agent-science half. Its cybernetics, ecology and systems half sits far out.
sector:life.missing: Nothing translates the systems half of the tradition into AI-safety research. Its 16 cybernetics, systems and ecology entries have no core organisation and none on the classic map, 9 are potential, and most only convene. Across all 49 entries the tradition also contributes nothing to protecting minds or meaning, and has only one entry whose primary problem is assurance.

cell_notes.note: No ring cell in this tradition is empty or holds two or fewer entries (core 10, bridge 13, adjacent 8, potential 18), so these notes cover the thin cells inside each ring. In core, cybernetics has 0 entries and biology 1 (softmax). The cybernetics zero is a real opening: the complexity notes found Equilibria Network's Viable System Model posts were the only explicit cybernetics-for-alignment work. The biology figure is also real: the Levin lab is bridge, and the biology notes found that three organisations (Softmax, Princint, ACS) carry almost all the traffic. Core also has no entry on systemic risk, security, justice, minds or meaning. That follows from the split between the two halves and is not a search miss.

Complexity has 1 bridge entry (concordia, a DeepMind software library) and biology 2 (levin-lab, nooma-labs). The complexity gap is mostly real. The big complexity institutes (santa-fe-institute, complexity-science-hub-vienna) were checked and have no AI-risk programme, so they sit in adjacent; NECSI was not verified, so a small artefact is possible. The biology figure is probably real. Google's Paradigms of Intelligence team could not be fetched, but it would be excluded as a lab programme anyway. Neuro looks healthy with 7 entries, but most are brain-inspired AGI programmes that double as capability bets (Astera Obelisk, WBAI, BrainCog, Eon). There is no NeuroAI-for-safety fellowship, although Neuromatch's own profile says one would fit its infrastructure.

Neuro has 0 adjacent entries and biology 1 (templeton-world-charity-foundation). The neuro zero is largely an artefact of the boundary rules. Neuroscience of what AI does to people is homed in psychology or law, with life as secondary (sapien-labs, winston-center-on-technology-and-brain-developme, neurorights-foundation). The same rule explains the empty life x minds problem cell. It is partly real all the same: the neuro notes found no neuroscience or psychiatry group working on AI-induced delusion, attachment or false attribution of consciousness. The empty life x meaning cell is real but expected, since that work sits in contemplative and religious homes (mind-life-institute, human-energy).

Complexity has 0 potential entries and neuro 1 (carboncopies-foundation). The complexity zero is very probably a search artefact. The complexity angle ran only 7 web queries before the shared budget ran out, and candidates such as NECSI, IIASA's systemic-risk work, Princeton's Global Systemic Risk group and Oxford INET were never checked or failed to load. The neuro figure is part artefact, part rule. The big neuroscience funders and societies (Kavli, Simons, Allen, ASSC) were noted as having no AI-safety window but not profiled, and consciousness bodies go to AI minds. By region the tradition has nothing in Africa or MENA, and its only Latin American entry is TWCF's nominal Bahamas base. That is likely a limit of English-only search, though ALife and complexity groups in Brazil, Mexico and Chile exist and are worth a sweep.

sector:life.key_insight: The tradition splits into two halves that study the same thing, self-regulating wholes, but face opposite ways. All 10 core entries and all 7 classic-map entries sit in the agent-science half (neuroscience, biology, complexity), which works mainly into the model (21 of 49 entries) and mainly on agency (19 primary). The 16 cybernetics, systems and ecology entries have no core entry, none on the classic map, and 9 at potential, and their focus is civilisational systemic risk (15 primary across the tradition). Equilibria Network, applying Stafford Beer's Viable System Model to gradual disempowerment, is almost the only organisation standing in both.

openings.title: Safety science for open-ended AI, built with the artificial-life community
openings.summary: Frontier labs now pursue open-ended, self-improving systems, an idea artificial life has studied for three decades. Yet no organisation owns the safety of open-ended search, and the field's learned society has no AI-safety track. A standing workshop at ALIFE 2027 in Prague, co-run with ACS, followed by a small research group, would bring that knowledge across.
openings.detail: ISAL is tagged as having no AI work at all, even though its field holds the deepest knowledge of open-ended evolution: novelty measures, major transitions, and how evolving populations escape their designers' intentions. On the ML side the topic exists only as papers: Ecoffet, Clune and Lehman (2020), a 2025 ICLR workshop paper arguing that safety is essential for open-ended systems, and a 2026 ICML position paper from CISPA. None of these is a programme, and none draws on ALife's community. NOOMA Labs (Kyoto) argues in PNAS Nexus that a diverse ecosystem of AI agents is a safer target than full alignment, and Japan's ALIGN draws on ALife, so the intellectual seeds are there. Success would be a recurring ALIFE workshop, a shared benchmark for open-ended search that stays within agreed bounds, and a three-to-five-person group whose alumni move into labs and safety institutes. The main risk is that safety-of-open-endedness work slides into capability work, since open-endedness is itself a frontier capability agenda. The ALife community may also resist x-risk framing.
steps: Approach the ALIFE 2027 organisers (Prague, 19-23 July 2027) together with ACS Research at Charles University, Prague, to propose a workshop on the safety of open-ended systems.
Commission a short review mapping what artificial life knows about steering and bounding open-ended evolution onto current lab agendas (self-improving agents, automated-scientist systems).
Fund two or three ALife researchers through an explicit open-endedness stream of the PIBBSS fellowship run by Principles of Intelligence.
If the workshop draws well, seed a small group at NOOMA Labs or as a Prague node alongside ACS.
openings.evidence: international-society-for-artificial-life is tagged transfer none_yet. The biology angle notes state that 'no organisation owns its safety'. life_biology has 8 potential entries but only 1 core (softmax). A quick web search found ML-side position papers (ICLR 2025 workshop, ICML 2026) but no organisation or ALife-side programme.

openings.title: A co-funded call bringing comparative cognition into AI agency and deception evals
openings.summary: Evaluators now have to judge whether an AI system really has a goal, knows it is being tested, or intends to deceive, and they risk both over- and under-attribution. Comparative cognition has spent a century building controls against exactly this error in animals. A joint call from Templeton's Diverse Intelligences hubs and a safety funder would pair those labs with evaluation teams.
openings.detail: In October 2025 TWCF committed nearly $2.8M to three Diverse Intelligences hubs. The St Andrews hub (GRCDI, about $1.2M for 2025-27) gives seed grants of up to £40k, but there is no safety track. DISI trains ML researchers alongside animal-cognition and cultural-evolution scientists, also without a safety track, and Berlin's SCIoI was renewed for 2026-2032. The bridge exists only in papers: Cambridge's Animal-AI environment and the 2025 paper 'Bringing Comparative Cognition to Computers'. Meanwhile UK AISI and independent evaluators face situational-awareness, sandbagging and scheming questions that are at heart attribution problems. Success would be six to ten pilot projects in which comparative cognitivists design the missing control conditions for evaluations of goal-directedness and test-awareness, with at least one method adopted by a safety institute. The risks: tasks built for animals may not carry over to text-based models, Templeton may resist an x-risk framing (framing the call around 'what kind of mind is this?' helps), and evaluation teams have little spare capacity.
steps: Approach GRCDI's co-directors (Josep Call, Amanda Seed) about a themed seed-grant round on AI agency and deception, matched by a safety funder (SFF, Longview, Coefficient Giving or UK AISI's Alignment Project).

Run a three-day workshop pairing about ten comparative cognitivists with evaluators from UK AISI and independent evaluation groups. Its output would be a list of control conditions missing from current scheming and situational-awareness evaluations.
Propose an AI-evaluation project strand for DISI 2027, drawing on its mixed ML and animal-cognition cohort.
openings.evidence: templeton-world-charity-foundation, global-research-centre-for-diverse-intelligences and diverse-intelligences-summer-institute are all convening-only, with no safety track. Only 1 of 49 life entries has assurance as its primary problem (gaia-network). life_biology has 8 potential entries. The biology notes name Templeton the largest funder in diverse intelligence. A web search found papers (Animal-AI, 2025 arXiv) but no standing programme.

openings.title: An ecology lab for populations of deployed AI agents
openings.summary: Large numbers of interacting AI agents are now deployed, yet nobody studies them as populations: what selection pressures act on them, how conformity cascades form, and when an agent ecosystem tips. Collective-behaviour biologists, evolutionary game theorists and cultural evolutionists already have these tools. A dedicated lab, partly staffed from Konstanz's collective-behaviour cluster as its funding ends, would apply them.
openings.detail: Konstanz's CASCB (more than 160 researchers) published work in August 2026 showing that capable LLM agents coordinate by following the majority in groups far larger than humans manage. The cluster was not renewed in the May 2025 Excellence Strategy decision, so its funding runs out in 2027 and skilled people will be looking for a home. MPI Plön and IT:U Linz (Hilbe: LLM strategies in the repeated prisoner's dilemma), Teesside (Han: evolutionary game theory of AI races), MPIB's Center for Humans and Machines (machine behaviour) and the Cultural Evolution Society (no AI activity, though members co-wrote 'Machine Culture') hold complementary methods. The tradition's multi-agent work in core and bridge either builds models (Softmax, XOR Labs) or simulates (Concordia, Equilibria); none observes real deployed populations. The Cooperative AI Foundation, which funds multi-agent risk research, is a natural co-funder. Success would be population-level monitoring of real agent ecosystems, early-warning indicators of cascades, and an ecology-grounded taxonomy of multi-agent failure. The risks: platforms control access to deployment data, there is overlap with cooperative-AI groups, and the analogy can stretch too far (agents are copied, not bred), so the lab must test which biological mechanisms actually hold.
steps: Talk to CASCB's leadership and David Garcia's group about which researchers face the 2027 funding end and would join an AI-agent-populations project.
Seek co-funding from the Cooperative AI Foundation and SFF for a two-year pilot of four to six researchers.
Propose an applied working group on machine culture to the Cultural Evolution Society, which invites proposals for new working groups.
Negotiate data access with at least one agent platform or marketplace before hiring.
openings.evidence: centre-for-the-advanced-study-of-collective-beha and max-planck-institute-for-evolutionary-biology-de are potential, and cultural-evolution-society is none_yet. In life x multi_agent, the 4 core and 4 bridge entries are model-builders or simulators, there are 0 adjacent entries, and the 2 potential entries are the Konstanz and Plön groups above. CASCB's funding ends in 2027. A web search for ecology of AI agents returned only AI-for-ecology work.

openings.title: Make homeostatic, bounded objectives a funded alignment research programme
openings.summary: The idea that an agent should regulate towards 'enough' rather than maximise has deep roots in physiology, in Ashby's cybernetics and in Bateson's critique of conscious purpose. By 2026 it had surfaced in alignment from three independent directions. Yet its only benchmarks are kept up by volunteers, and a modest grant programme would turn it into a testable research line.
openings.detail: Aintelope (core) maintains open-source gridworld benchmarks for homeostasis, bounded and multiple objectives, diminishing returns and resource sharing, and probes when LLM agents collapse into unbounded maximisation. Its profile describes the agentic work as largely volunteer. The Levin lab's 2026 preprint proposes homeostatic objectives by analogy with cancer as cellular misalignment. PIK's BeGa group (Heitzig) publishes on non-maximising, empowerment-preserving agents, and Byrnes at Astera works on social instincts as an alignment target. The source knowledge sits with cyberneticians (the-cybernetics-society, american-society-for-cybernetics) and the Bateson lineage (international-bateson-institute, no AI work at all), and none of them is connected to alignment. Success would be a maintained benchmark suite cited by labs or safety institutes, and evidence on whether agents trained towards bounded objectives resist the drift into maximising. For int/a it is the clearest technical form of 'moving at the speed of wisdom'. The risks are known: a bounded objective can be unstable as capability grows, or be gamed, and the line could stay niche.
steps: A funder offers Aintelope a 12-18 month grant (roughly $150-300k) to professionalise and maintain the benchmarks and add a track for LLM agents.

Convene a small workshop of Aintelope, the Levin lab, PIK's BeGa group, Steve Byrnes and three or four cyberneticians from the Cybernetics Society and ASC, to write a joint research agenda on non-maximising agents.
Ask Principles of Intelligence to run a PIBBSS fellowship stream on homeostasis and regulation, recruiting from physiology and cybernetics.
openings.evidence: aintelope (core) is volunteer-run, and the biology angle notes list homeostatic objectives as having 'only volunteer-scale work'. life_cybernetics has 16 entries and 0 in core. levin-lab-allen-discovery-center-at-tufts-univer and potsdam-institute-for-climate-impact-research published on the idea in 2026. international-bateson-institute is tagged none_yet. A search found Aintelope's benchmark paper and Alignment Forum posts but no funded programme.

sector:indigenous.overview: This tradition gives the safety field two things it lacks. The first is working tools for collective consent, provenance and community authority over data and models: the CARE Principles, IEEE 2890-2025, the TK and BC Labels and the Kaitiakitanga Licence. The second is a set of relational ontologies that approach AI through kinship, reciprocity and obligation instead of control. Its 15 home organisations fall into two groups. Indigenous-led knowledge and data-sovereignty bodies: abundant-intelligences, te-hiku-media, global-indigenous-data-alliance, te-mana-raraunga-m-ori-data-sovereignty-network, local-contexts and old-ways-new. Decolonial, Black and feminist groups: distributed-ai-research-institute, masakhane, coding-rights, a-alliance-for-inclusive-algorithms-and-the-femi and technecultura. Six other organisations draw on the tradition as a secondary one (tattle-civic-tech, it-for-change, lavits, bioneers, science-and-nonduality, histories-of-artificial-intelligence). It sits further from the AI-safety core than any other tradition on the map. It has no core entries and one bridge (Old Ways, New, through its founder's reviewer seat on the International AI Safety Report). None of its organisations is on the aisafety.com map.
